messages:
Nishant: :rotating_light: Paging oncall — multiple customers reporting 5xx and timeouts for inference in eu-central-1. Seeing a spike in econnreset and long tail latencies. Rooting thread here.
PagerDutyBot: Incident INC-2026-834 created and assigned to Nishant. Priority: P1.
Nishant: Observed across multiple deploys: p50 latency from 220ms -> 1.2s, p95 1.8s+, and 5xx rate climbed from 0.3% -> ~12% over last 7m. Instances in eu-central-1a show lots of ENI flaps and transient NAT failures.
Chris: Confirming, net logs show repeated ENI detach/attach events and some host-level kernel logs with `NETDEV_DOWN` around the same time. Could be a networking backend issue in that AZ.
Jordan: Traffic patterns: we had a small traffic spike, but autoscaling handled CPU/GPUs fine. This is network-bound — tails and connection churn.
Ellen: Any customer-facing impact notes? A few mid-market customers hit errors in the last 10m, some reduced throughput, one customer reported queued requests in their app.
Nishant: Putting mitigation steps: 1) short-term: route traffic away from eu-central-1a to eu-central-1b/c and eu-west-1; 2) enable faster fallbacks for critical customers; 3) open AWS ticket for zonal networking.
InfraBot: Runbook step: `rw-route status --region eu-central-1 --az eu-central-1a` shows degraded. Suggested action: `rw-route promote --exclude-az eu-central-1a --grace 30s`.
Chris: I'm going to scale down or mark hosts in eu-central-1a as drained for the routing plane so new connections avoid them. Will run a soft drain first: `kc exec routing-controller -- rwctl drain-az eu-central-1a --soft`.
Nishant: Also toggling DNS fallback TTL to 15s for the next 30m to let clients pick up alternate endpoints faster. Command:```
# emergency TTL change
redwood-dns update --zone redwood-prod --record api.prod.redwood.ai --ttl 15
```
Jordan: Note: DNS TTL change helps external clients but our internal smart-router uses region weights. I'm going to adjust weights:```
# shift 60% traffic off eu-central-1a
rwctl set-region-weight --region eu-central-1 --az-weight eu-central-1a=0.2,eu-central-1b=0.5,eu-central-1c=0.3
```
Ellen: I've notified Customer Ops and posted a status update draft for affected customers. Suggest calling out that we're rerouting traffic and working with AWS.
Chris: Soft drain in progress — removing new sessions from eu-central-1a. Will monitor connection count and queue sizes.
Nishant: PagerDuty acknowledged by Nishant. Handoff to Chris for infra mitigation. I'll handle customer comms and cross-region routing changes.
InfraBot: AWS console event: `ENI detachment rate increased in eu-central-1a` (internal alert). Ticket created with AWS support (case 7891123).
Jordan: Observability: KV cache hit rate dropped ~15% for sessions moved off-az (expected); we should anticipate slight latency increase for those users due to cache warmup. Consider enabling KV cache warming for critical routes.
Chris: Action: enabling routing fallback to use cached/k-ngram-friendly model variant for 60s to reduce token churn. Config applied: `model-fallback --policy cheap-fast --duration 60s`.
Nishant: Quick customer triage: two customers on Dedicated capacity in eu-central-1a — one has isolation in same AZ. Reached out to SEs; recommending they promote failover to their reserved eu-central-1b pools.
Ellen: Customer Ops update sent. Logged affected customers and suggested mitigations.
Jordan: Metrics after reroute (~4m): 5xx down to 3.8%, p95 latency 1.1s -> 520ms, connection churn reducing. Good sign.
Nishant: Good. Keep drains running until AWS confirms stable. Also capturing logs for postmortem: `s3://redwood-incident-logs/inc-2026-834/`.
Chris: AWS responded: they see a fabric issue in eu-central-1a's network plane affecting ENI attachments. They have engineers engaged and will update ETA within 30m.
PagerDutyBot: Reminder: on-call rotation — Nishant will hand off to Jordan in 30 minutes for monitoring.
Nishant: Handoff note: Jordan will own until AWS confirms fix and eu-central-1a is back to normal. Key things to watch: ENI attach rate, NAT gateway error rate, open connections, and 5xx.
Jordan: Acknowledged. I have dashboards pinned and alerts lowered to noisier thresholds for faster detection. Also keeping DNS TTL low for 1h.
Ellen: Customer Ops will keep customers updated every 30m until resolved.
Chris: Patchwork: I'm leaving 2 healthy nodes in eu-central-1a to handle sticky sessions; all new traffic should avoid the problematic AZ.
Nishant: Postmortem items initial list: timeline, root cause (AWS fabric/ENI issue), mitigation effectiveness (routing weights, TTL change, model fallback), customer impact list, and follow-ups with AWS for SLA credit.
InfraBot: Incident status changed to "Mitigating".
Jordan: 20m after initial page: 5xx down to 0.7%, p95 ~340ms, system stable for now. Will keep monitoring and reconvene if any regressions.
Nishant: Thanks team. If AWS fixes AZ, we'll slowly reintroduce capacity and bump weights back over 10m windows. Leaving this thread open for postmortem notes. :thumbsup:
Ellen: Adding link to status page and customer list in ticket.
Chris: Leaving small checklist here: `1) confirm AWS fix; 2) validate no residual ENI flaps; 3) resume normal weights; 4) run traffic soak; 5) write postmortem`
PagerDutyBot: Incident INC-2026-834 status: Mitigated — monitoring.
Jordan: I'll take final watch and close when all metrics are healthy for 60m.
Nishant: Closing handoff. Thanks all.
